problem: Prior map-based navigation work mostly proposes ways to build and use maps under imperfect localization. Nobody had systematically tested what information in a map actually helps navigation, or how learned egocentric maps compare with oracle maps and with no map as task horizon grows. Existing multi-object tasks (SMT's object search, ordered k-item) use fixed goal sets, do not control object placement, and have no explicit FOUND action, so their difficulty cannot be controlled.
motivation: Embodied agents that nearly solve PointNav become brittle when paths lengthen or more locations must be visited, so memory is a key bottleneck for long-horizon navigation. The paper assumes perfect localization and uses a deliberately simple base task. This separates 'what is useful to store in a map' from mapping noise and from confounders such as language or scene priors. Episode difficulty can be dialed up by adding goals.
key_idea: Define MultiON, an ObjectGoal generalization where the agent must find an episode-specific ordered sequence of m inserted colored-cylinder objects in Habitat/MP3D and call FOUND at each. Then benchmark a common PPO/GRU agent that differs only in its memory: no map, oracle maps, oracle-egocentric maps, or learned maps.
insight: Goal-object semantics in the map, not occupancy, drives the gain. OracleMap (Obj) reaches 94/82/59 SR on 1/2/3-ON versus 66/34/16 for OracleMap (Occ); the authors attribute occupancy's small value to perfect depth and localization already handling collisions. A naive map that stores classifier-predicted goal categories at the agent's cell (ObjRecogMap) beats MapNet-style neural feature maps (ProjNeuralMap, EgoMap) on 1-ON and 2-ON. The backtracking analysis shows why: map agents find the k-th goal much more often if it was seen earlier (ObjRecogMap +19/+25 points; NoMap/OracleMap only +1–2). The ablations point to the FOUND decision and multi-goal disambiguation as the bottlenecks. Allowing OracleMap a single wrong FOUND raises 3-ON SR from 48 to 66. A dynamically updated oracle map that shows only the current goal gets 94/85/81 SR versus 94/74/48, so performance drops faster than exponentially with m.
method: MultiON task: m-ON episodes with m goals sampled without replacement from 8 colored cylinders (h 0.75 m, r 0.05 m) inserted into MP3D scenes. Geodesic distance from start to goal 1 and between successive goals is 2–20 m. The agent must call FOUND near each goal in order; a wrong FOUND ends the episode; max 2,500 steps.
Metrics: Success (all goals in order), Progress (fraction of goals found), SPL over the concatenated shortest path through all goals, and PPL (progress-weighted path length).

Base agent: RGB-D 256x256 goes through a CNN and a linear layer; the egocentric map crop goes through a CNN and a linear layer; 16-d embeddings of the goal one-hot and previous action are added. The concatenation feeds a GRU, then an actor-critic head. Trained with PPO for 40M frames (16 threads, 4 mini-batches, 2 epochs). Reward is r_goal=3.0 on correct FOUND, plus decrease in geodesic distance, plus slack α=−0.01.

Oracle maps: OracleMap is a 300x300 GT global map with 0.8 m cells and learned 16-d embeddings for occupancy (navigable / non-navigable / outside) and goal category (k+1 classes). OracleEgoMap reveals that same map progressively via ray tracing within a 79° FOV, 5 m range and occlusion.

ObjRecogMap (learned): an auxiliary (k+1)-way classifier on the RGB frame, supervised with GT goal category via cross-entropy, predicts which goal is in view (within 79° FOV and 2.5 m). The predicted category embedding is written into the global map cell at the agent's position.

ProjNeuralMap / EgoMap (learned): MapNet-style depth-conditioned projection of CNN image features into a 7x13 egocentric grid. It is registered into the global map using the known pose, with element-wise max-pooling. EgoMap adds an attention-based map read (after Beeching et al.).
Implicit-memory and random baselines: NoMap(RNN) (GRU only), FRMQN (key-value memory with soft attention), SMT (transformer over stored observation embeddings), Rand, and Rand+OracleFound.

setting.backbone: CNN encoders + GRU actor-critic, trained from scratch with PPO (ObjRecogMap adds an auxiliary object-category classifier)
setting.training_data: MultiON train split generated on Matterport3D train scenes: 50,000 episodes per scene for each of 1-ON/2-ON/3-ON. Each agent is trained for 40M frames on each m-ON task. The ObjRecogMap classifier is supervised with GT goal categories at train time.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (256x256) + current goal one-hot + previous action; map agents additionally use the perfect agent pose for map registration
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN-LEFT / TURN-RIGHT 30° / FOUND
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D scenes with inserted cylinder goal objects)
setting.privileged: Perfect localization (GT pose) and noise-free sensing/actuation for all agents. OracleMap uses the full GT occupancy + goal-location map; OracleEgoMap uses the GT map revealed by visibility. Learned-map agents (ObjRecogMap, ProjNeuralMap) use GT pose only.

numbers_note: This is a benchmark paper, so all agents are the authors' implementations. Only ObjRecogMap, ProjNeuralMap, OracleEgoMap and OracleMap (Occ+Obj) are listed. Other Table 2 rows (Test SR / Progress / SPL / PPL for 1/2/3-ON) are: NoMap(RNN) 62/24/10 | 62/39/24 | 35/13/4 | 35/21/14; FRMQN 62/29/13 | 62/42/29 | 50/24/11 | 50/33/24; SMT 63/28/9 | 63/44/22 | 48/26/7 | 48/36/18; EgoMap 69/46/26 | 69/59/44 | 49/31/18 | 49/42/30; OracleMap (Obj) 94/82/59 | 94/86/70 | 79/65/42 | 79/67/50; OracleMap (Occ) 66/34/16 | 66/47/36 | 48/25/12 | 48/35/27. Appendix Tables 6–9 add further ablations: DynamicOracleMap SR 94/85/81; OnlyOracleMap SR 54/9/0; OracleMapHiddenObjects SR 91/72/40; FOUND-budget sweep; shape-varied targets. There are text/table inconsistencies. The text quotes OracleMap 'SUCCESS rates are 0.94, 0.79 and 0.62', which match the Progress column; Table 2 SR is 94/74/48. The text's 'OracleMap success drops to only 59% (42% SPL) for 3-ON' corresponds to the OracleMap (Obj) row. Some Table 5 generalization entries (e.g., OracleEgoMap trained on 2-ON evaluated on 1-ON = 8, relative −3) look like typos. Training curves appear only in figures. This paper's MultiON dataset (8 colored cylinders, MP3D) differs from later MultiON challenge versions.
results: Performance collapses as goals are added: even OracleMap drops from 94% SR on 1-ON to 74% on 2-ON and 48% on 3-ON, and OracleMap (Obj) reaches 59% SR / 42% SPL on 3-ON. Explicit maps clearly beat implicit memory; FRMQN is the best no-map model at 62/29/13 SR. Among learned maps, the simple ObjRecogMap (79/51/22 SR) beats ProjNeuralMap (70/45/27) and EgoMap (69/46/26) on 1-ON and 2-ON but not on 3-ON. It still trails OracleEgoMap (83/64/37). Random search with an oracle FOUND gets only 26/8/2 SR, and pure Rand gets 0.
limitations: Assumes perfect localization and noise-free depth/actuation, so the results do not show how maps fare under real SLAM/odometry noise; only grid maps are studied, not topological maps.
Goals are synthetic colored cylinders inserted into MP3D scenes rather than natural objects; varying shape instead of color changes results markedly (NoMap 3-ON SR 10 → 0).

The hard FOUND termination dominates failures (one extra allowed wrong FOUND lifts OracleMap 3-ON SR 48→66). Test evaluation uses only 1,000 episodes, and agents trained on 1-ON fail to generalize to more goals.
builds_on: Habitat ObjectGoal navigation (Anderson et al. evaluation guidelines)
